faq: Do I need to know code to use the components?
No. We build them with property controls, so you change text, colors and options in the Framer panel just as you would for built-in elements.
Will custom code slow my site?
We keep code small and load it only where it is needed. We check the page speed before and after, and we avoid heavy libraries when a few lines will do.
Can you copy an effect from another site?
We can build a similar effect from your description. We do not copy another site's code or protected design, and we write our own implementation.
What if Framer changes and breaks a component?
We build with supported Framer code methods to reduce the risk. If an update affects it after our fix window, our management service or a small order can repair it.

desc:
Custom Framer components and code overrides add the interactive parts that the standard Framer tools cannot make. Ecom Swift LLC builds pricing calculators, filtered galleries, sliders, cursors and scroll effects as reusable pieces with controls you can edit on the canvas.

## What are Framer components and code overrides?

A Framer component is a reusable block, built visually or in code, that you can place on any page and adjust through its properties. A code override is a small piece of code that changes how an existing layer behaves, for example adding a scroll effect or a click action.

Components suit things you use in several places. Overrides suit one-off behavior on a single element. We choose between them based on what you need to edit later.

## Why custom parts are sometimes the right answer

Framer covers a wide range of layouts and animations without code. Some ideas fall outside that range: a calculator that reacts to user input, a gallery that filters by tag, a slider that compares two images, or a block that pulls live data from an outside source.

The usual workarounds are poor. Pasting an embed from a third party can add weight and break the styling. Faking an interaction with many stacked layers makes a project hard to maintain. A purpose-built component does the job once, matches the site and stays editable.

## How good components affect your site

Interactive elements help visitors understand an offer faster. A pricing calculator lets a buyer see a number for their own case. A before and after slider shows a result without a paragraph of explanation. A filtered gallery lets people jump to work that matches their need.

Quality matters here because the cost of a poor component is high. Heavy scripts slow every page that loads them. Parts that ignore keyboard users or motion preferences exclude real visitors. We build for light loading, clear states and accessible behavior, so the feature helps instead of getting in the way.

## What a well-made Framer component includes

- Property controls, so you change text, colors, sizes and content in the editor without opening code.
- Variants for states such as default, hover, active and disabled.
- Layout that adapts to phone, tablet and desktop widths.
- Styling that matches your fonts, colors and spacing.
- Keyboard access and visible focus for interactive parts.
- A reduced-motion setting for animation-heavy pieces.
- Small file weight and no unneeded libraries.
- Sensible empty and error states when data fails to load.
- Testing in the main browsers.
- A short usage note with examples of how to place and configure it.

## How we work

You describe the behavior you want, and, if you have one, send an example of the effect you have in mind. We confirm the scope in plain terms: what the part does, what you can edit and what it will not do. We then build it inside a copy of your project, test it at all screen sizes and share a preview.

Basic covers one component or override with editable controls. Standard adds up to a few components that share one style, with variants and keyboard support. Premium covers a small library, a live data feed or API call, custom scroll and hover interactions, a reduced-motion option, a guide with examples and a period of fixes after delivery.

We write original code for your project. If you point us at an effect on another site, we recreate the behavior in our own way, not copy someone else's code.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Describe what the visitor should be able to do, not just how it looks.
- Share the content that will fill the component, since real content exposes layout problems.
- Decide what you want to edit yourself, so we expose those controls.
- Test the finished part on your own phone.
- Keep a list of which pages use which component.

**Avoid:**
- Adding custom code for something Framer already does well.
- Stacking several heavy effects on one page.
- Relying on hover alone, since phones have no hover.
- Pulling in large outside libraries for a small feature.
- Asking for animation that cannot be turned down for visitors who prefer less motion.

## Who this is for

This service suits a studio that wants a signature interaction on its home page, a software company that needs a calculator or interactive demo, and a store or portfolio owner who wants a filtered gallery. It also helps a team whose Framer project needs one missing part before a launch.

## What we need from you

Send a clear description of the behavior, any reference links or screenshots, the content that will go inside, and the page where it will live. Invite us as a collaborator on your Framer project, so the work happens in your own account. We never ask for passwords.

If the component needs data from an outside service, tell us which one. You will need to supply the access details through that service's own sharing tools, never by sending a login.
